## 1256 N Artesian Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 16012280180000 | West Town (Community Area 24) | Ward 26**

> **Note:** This parcel is currently **city-owned** (status: "Owned by City / Interest") and is **tax-exempt** (class EX). Any acquisition or development would require engaging the City of Chicago. Assessment data is not available for this parcel in its current use; a change of ownership or use would trigger reassessment.

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RM-4.5** (Residential Multi-Unit), per the City's GIS parcel records. The district was set by ordinance A7210, dated September 5, 2007; the map was last edited October 27, 2021. This is **authoritative** — the PIN was matched directly to county address records.

**Verify:** [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) | Governing code: [1] (§17-2-0104)

---

### 2. Is 3+ Unit Residential Permitted By Right?

**Yes.** RM-4.5 expressly allows multi-unit residential buildings — the permitted uses include detached houses, two-flats, townhouses, and multi-unit buildings [1]. Three or more units is permitted by right, subject to the bulk and density standards below. No special use or Planned Development is required.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

All figures are from the zoning table for RM-4.5 [1] (§17-2-0104) and the density standards at [2] (§17-2-0303-A):

| Standard | RM-4.5 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 1.7 |
| **Max Height** | 45–47 ft (varies by lot frontage) |
| **Min Lot Area per Dwelling Unit** | 700 sq ft |
| **Min Lot Size** | 1,650 sq ft |

**Setbacks:** The retrieved code text [3] (§17-10-0600) addresses parking setbacks in RS districts; RM-district side-setback rules appear at [4] (§17-3-0400 cross-references RM context). The RM-4.5 base district requires no front or side setback by default for multi-unit buildings, but **confirm specific setback figures** directly in §17-2-0400 of the Municipal Code — the exact RM setback table was not returned in the retrieved text.

*Code vintage: current through the Council Journal of March 18, 2026.*

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

**a. Predominance of the Block (606) District**
This parcel is within this special district, but it **does not apply here** — it affects only RS-3 and RT-3.5 parcels, allowing a two-unit building at 1,500 sq ft per unit in those single-family zones. Your RM-4.5 zoning is unaffected [2] (§17-2-0303-B.1); detail also at the overlay's code link: §17-7-0591.

**b. ADU-Allowed RS Area — Zone 1**
The parcel sits in an ADU-Allowed RS Area with **no limitations** [1] (§17-7-0570–0574). However, because this parcel is RM-4.5 (not an RS district), coach houses and conversion units are already **permitted by right** under the RM district standards at §17-2-0207 — no special ADU overlay is needed.

**c. Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone**
This parcel is in an ARO Zone. Any residential development of **10 or more units** (or receiving city financial assistance at lower thresholds) will trigger affordable unit requirements. West Town has 20 ARO-tracked projects with 291 total affordable units in the community area. Confirm current ARO thresholds and requirements with the Department of Housing.

**d. No Planned Development, Landmark, Historic District, Lakefront Protection, or PMD** — none apply.

**e. Transit Access (not TOD-designated)**
The nearest CTA rail is **Damen Blue Line**, 0.67 miles away. The nearest Metra is **Western Ave (Milwaukee North)**, 1.07 miles away. The parcel is **not TOD-eligible** under the Connected Communities Ordinance, so no parking reduction under that program applies here.

**f. Flood Zone:** FEMA Zone X — area of minimal flood hazard. No flood insurance requirement.

**g. No SSA, no TIF, no Opportunity Zone, no Enterprise Zone** apply to this parcel.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement

RM district off-street parking must be located on the same zoning lot as the dwellings served [3] (§17-10-0602-B). Parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within a 20-foot front setback [3] (§17-10-0602-A).

The specific **automobile parking ratio** for RM-4.5 was not returned in the retrieved code text (the parking ratio table retrieved covers D-district residential uses [5] — §17-10-0200). Confirm the RM-4.5 minimum ratio at §17-10-0200 in the full Municipal Code. Because this parcel is **not TOD-eligible**, no transit-proximity parking reduction applies.

---

### 6. Maximum Units By Right — Can You Build 6?

**By lot-area-per-unit math: 4 units by right. 6 units is not supported by lot area alone.**

The arithmetic from the zoning table [1] (§17-2-0303-A): 3,191 sq ft ÷ 700 sq ft per unit = **4.56 → 4 units** (fractional units round down). This is a hard lot-area ceiling under RM-4.5 at this lot size.

**Could you build 6?** Not by right at 700 sq ft/unit on 3,191 sq ft. To reach 6 units you would need either:
- **Efficiency or SRO units**, which count at a smaller lot-area figure than standard dwelling units [2] (§17-2-0303, lot_area_note; §17-2-0104 density table) — confirm the exact efficiency/SRO lot-area-per-unit in the full density table at §17-2-0200;
- A **Planned Development** or zoning map amendment to a denser district; or
- Ground-floor **Type A accessible units**, which are exempt from the per-unit calculation in RS-3, RT-3.5, and RT-4 [2] (§17-2-0303-B.2) — but that exemption is listed only for those districts, **not RM-4.5**, so do not rely on it here without further confirmation.

**Also note:** FAR (1.7 × 3,191 sq ft = ~5,425 sq ft of floor area) and the height limit (45–47 ft) are independent constraints that could further limit unit count regardless of lot area.

**Verify all of the above:** Full zoning code at §17-2-0200 (density table), §17-2-0303, and §17-2-0400 (setbacks) via the [Municipal Code of Chicago](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/) or contact the Chicago Zoning Department at (312) 744-5777.

---

**Confidence:** High on zoning district, permitted uses, FAR, height, and lot-area unit yield (all from authoritative parcel and code data). **Could not confirm** from retrieved text: exact RM-4.5 parking ratio, precise front/rear setback dimensions, and whether the efficiency/SRO lot-area figure would get you to 6 units — those require the full §17-2-0200 density table. City-ownership status is a critical threshold issue to resolve before any development planning.
